notes.title: Launch Day Feedback: We are listening!
notes.content:
(German translation/deutsche Übersetzung)

One of the great parts about indie development is that there is a very accessible and close connection between developers and players, i.e. we don’t have to go through mounds of paperwork and oodles of meetings to get things done. 

One of the great parts about launching on such a large gaming portal like Steam is that our game is fanned in front of thousands of eyes, and in turn we get some great feedback, all of which is great! If it is a heartfelt thanks, or a crushingly negative review, it is still feedback and it is still great for us to hear. We think the best way to make any game great is to have a two way street of communication with players and consider all feedback, even the negative.

In turn, when you combine the quick turnaround speed that indie development offers, along with all of the great new feedback, it means our game will begin to get buffed and shined, and we will end up with a gem in no time. 

We have been on the forums, Steam chat, YouTube, hanging out in game, reading player reviews, and keeping our ears to the ground everywhere we can think of. 

We know it’s only been one day, but here is what we have learned so far, and more importantly, here is what we are going to do about it.

Attack While Moving We have heard several players ask to be able to move and attack at the same time. This requires a bit of tech and new animations to make happen, but we think this would be a move in a positive direction. We have IMMEDIATELY started our artists on this task.

Controls: Several players have made note of both AD strafe (vs QE strafe) as well as the jerkiness of WASD. Again, we agree. We have already fixed for strafe, and will be looking at the WASD issues. These both should be live with our next build. 

Animations: We have received several suggestions that our character animations aren't expressive enough. Some of them feel clunky and out of date, particularly strafing. We agree. Our artists have started working on some new animations to really make our characters feel alive. 

Linearity of the starting zones: While the game does open up quite a bit after level 12-15, a lot of new players noted that the early zones felt very linear with little room for exploration. We agree. We are going to go through each of those zones and add a few secret and optional areas for players to discover. 

NPC Greetings: Our NPC’s greet players in several different languages. This was something that was intentionally done to add some variety to our game world. However many players have felt that this was some sort of localization bug, and others just plain don't like it. We are going to take steps to start cleaning these up to make them feel both more accurate to the server, as well as expressive of the NPC speaking.

Launcher Stability: We have had a lot of players having issues with the launcher either crashing or not launching the game. This will be one of our main priorities to fix. 

Dancing: Several players have asked for dancing animations for their character. It may be a small thing, but we think that would be great, and we have started working on it.

Additionally, these are things that we have heard from the community, and have already fixed (these changes are live):
The download was taking too long: We have fixed this. Our CDN was overloaded so we moved it to Amazon Cloudfront. Reports are that download speed has been increased.

Tutorial zones were overwhelmed: We have opened up more channels and instances in the zones to allow for more new players at one time. 

Respawn rates were too low: We lowered respawn times from 1.5 minutes down to 12 seconds. We will continue to monitor the tutorial zones as well as other high level zones and make tweaks as we need.

Quest tracker was broken: We fixed this.

Some new players got a ‘zone full’ message: We made a way for more tutorial channels to open. No player should see this message again!

We hope you can come along with us on Villagers and Heroes journey. We love live development, and we love working with players of all types. Leave your suggestions on the forums, or send us a PM on Steam. We would love to hear from you. 

-The Mad Otter Team

notes.title: Slaying Ghosts
notes.content:
Slaying Ghosts: How we boosted zone load by 5x

(German translation / deutsche Übersetzung) 

In a game like Villagers and Heroes, the game world is refereed by a central server (actually, many).  The central server makes sure all the players see the same thing on their computer.  Its job is to keep all the objects in the world synchronized across everyone’s computer.  

Take a look at this sample screen from the game:

http://i.imgur.com/z9PC91g.jpg

There are many objects in this scene: player avatars, monsters, trees, a lamp post, a road, a river, and so on.  All of those objects must be tracked.  Here’s a schematic drawing of what the server sees:
 
http://i.imgur.com/Xkyb9cM.jpg

I labelled these objects:
1. Player Avatar
2. Monster
3. Lamp Post
4. River
5.Tree(s) 
6. Bridge

The server has to make sure that all of these objects are in the exact same place on everyone’s computer.  So, to accomplish this, it transmits over the internet, each object’s type (tree, players, monster, etc.), and its location.

Here’s a new picture that shows this communication taking place between the server and one of the player’s computers.  A player’s computer is often called a client.

http://i.imgur.com/is435D7.jpg

Every arrow in this diagram represents a transmission that the server must make to ALL the clients in the game (at least to players who are near this location in the world).  (Side Note: There is only one arrow going from the Client back to the Server.  That’s because the only object that the Client has control over is the player’s avatar.)  Each of these arrows is expensive.  Hundreds of bytes must be transmitted per object per client.  This puts Load on the server-- it eats up CPU cycles and chews up Server bandwidth.  The consequence of this is that it can make the game appear “laggy” or sluggish.  And, possibly worse, it can take time for all the information to be transmitted from the server to the client.

The process of transmitting information about objects is called “ghosting”.  Each object in the scene exists in two places-- one on the server, and one on the client.  The copy on the server is considered the real object, and the copy that the server transmitted--or “ghosted”--is considered its ghost.

Finally, I should mention that this picture is simplified.  In a real situation, there are HUNDREDS of objects being ghosted from the server to the client.


What does the game Tribes have to do with Villagers and Heroes?
Now I want to take a brief detour.  The engine that Villagers and Heroes uses is Torque3D.  This a third-generation engine based on the game engine that Dynamix developed for the game “Tribes”.  Tribes is one of the most influential games in game history.  It was the first First Person Shooter game to feature powered battlesuits, team-based matches, and jump jets.  It’s the forerunner of games like HALO and TitanFall.  One area where it excelled was in its networking.  One of the design goals of Tribes was that every mission should be completely moddable.  Along with ability of any player to run their own server, it allowed the community to build their own custom missions.

However, one of the costs of having completely moddable missions, is that the server has to tell every client where everything is (and what everything is).

Look back at the picture that shows ghosting from server to client.  Most of the objects in that picture never move. Of all of those objects, the only objects that DO move are the player, and the monsters.  So, it is a waste that we are transmitting the types and positions of EVERY object in the scene.  A better solution is to have the Client load the types and positions of all the non-moving objects from the hard drive.  It is WAY faster to load from hard drive than receiving the information over the internet.  Additionally, when the player’s computer can handle all this work completely on its own, this saves the server a tremendous amount of work, cutting down on CPU and bandwidth usage.  Here is a schematic of what the new system looks like:

http://i.imgur.com/P7Khb9M.jpg

This is the system that Clark Fagot implemented for the game recently.  Red arrows increase load times and put load on the server, whereas green arrows load quickly and put no load on the server.


The Results
On average, it reduced the zone loading times for our players from 40 seconds to 8 seconds.  This is the difference between getting bored and keeping the gameplay rolling.  In addition, it saves bandwidth for the game servers, and all the players.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

http://i.imgur.com/UDP3BK0.png Eine deutsche Übersetzung dieses Artikels findet Ihr in unserem Forum:

Geister töten, oder wie wir es geschafft haben, die Zonenladezeiten um das Fünffache zu verkürzen.

notes.title: Monster Monday: Heartbruiser
notes.content:
Every Monday we release a new featured Bounty Boss, sharing a bit of lore and information about the Seven Realms most treacherous creatures. We are sharing our backlog of Monster Mondays for our Steam users to enjoy. 

http://i.imgur.com/r7zrDC8.png

Heartbruiser
Race: Ogre
Location: Deforested Forest

Heartbruiser’s tale begins many years ago, during a time when Heartbruiser decided to seek a bit of adventure (or possibly ‘adventurers’, most likely to snack on. His intentions were vague). And so the Ogre left his dark gloomy cave and set out into the forests of Greenhaven. Being a slightly intelligent ogre, Heartbruiser had the foresight to mark his route on trees as he ventured deeper into the wild forests of Greenhaven.

After months of roaming, and finding several tasty wargs, daggertooths, as well as a few low level humans, Heartbruiser decided that the adventuring life was not for him, and headed home.

Shortly after beginning his return trip, Heartbruiser came upon a sad sight indeed, the deforested Forest. This wouldn’t have been particularly sad to Heartbruiser, or any ogre for that matter, unless of course those exact trees had been intentionally marked, which indeed they were. The treacherous goblins of Greenhaven had wiped clean Heartbruisers carefully marked path, the Ogre was now lost. In a fit of rage Heartbruiser stormed and rampaged through the first encampment he found, destroying any small green humanoid that smelled of oil and wood shavings. But eventually his rage slowed, his energy dwindled, and Heartbruiser had to face the cold truth that he would be forever lost in this terrible pit of dead trees and goblin odor.

And so Heartbruiser roams the deforested forest, angry, sad, and then angry some more, looking for any victim that he could use to vent out a few punches of frustration.

notes.title: Monster Monday: Bully Bacon
notes.content:
Every Monday we release a new featured Bounty Boss, sharing a bit of lore and information about the Seven Realms most treacherous creatures. We are sharing our backlog of Monster Mondays for our Steam users to enjoy. 

https://i.imgur.com/9YTHibH.png

Bully Bacon
Race: Boar
Location: Elk Meadow

After moving to Ardent, Bully Bacon then became terribly aware of the vile nature of humans.

Every day thousands of humans would roll by his small nook of the city and simply kill him for sport. At first Bully Bacon thought this was because of all the experience that the humans were accumulating from their spars with him, but soon Bully Bacon realized a terrible truth… they weren’t. The amount of experience that humans were getting from him was negligible, and shortly after he realized that sometimes they would kill him simply hoping to find a piece of bacon to give some weirdo named Cyprian… times were bleak, and poor Bully Bacon hung his head in grief.

But then chance had it that King Leo decided to renovate the city, rebuilding it from the ground up. Bully Bacon came to realize that this was the perfect time for him to move back to the country. He packed up the few small things he owned, and in the midst of the chaos of construction, Bully slipped away.

With all of the experience of city life behind him, Bully Bacon grew in power, only a bit, but more than most bounty bosses ever do. He slipped into a quiet corner of Elk Meadow to live out his days. Of course he would still be killed on occasion, but these were much less frequent than before; overall Bully Bacon decided that he had found peace.

notes.title: Stats of V&H!
notes.content:
http://i.imgur.com/gVV12ci.png

Hello Everyone,

We thought some of you might like to see some of the statistics associated with Villagers and Heroes. We’ve put together a collection of stats, spanning across several different categories.



The Players:
362,000 characters have been created since Villagers and Heroes launched in 2011.
 
Gear, Feats, and Spells:
10,566 unique Spells, Feats, and Effects (including various ranks) 
43,000 different ways in which each class can choose to fill up their action bar with the 72 spells and feats available. This does not include ranks, which would make the number astronomically higher.
1,938,816,000 different ways that each class can use Gnogmenting to set up their gear with (rough estimate).
9198 Unique Items
1078 Different Weapons
3847 Different pieces of gear (belts, gloves, boots, outfits, hats, shields, rings, amulets)

The World and Monsters:
1393 Unique Bounty Bosses, 28 of which are Elder Bosses
110 Unique Zones, not including the 117 unique villages currently on live servers.
231 Unique Zingara (rare spawns).
2449 Unique normal monsters
13,303 separate locations for the baddies of the world to spawn

Crafting:
1381 unique recipes across 4 Crafting Skills (Tailoring, Smithing, Cooking, Woodcrafting)
6 Gathering skills (Gardening, Ranching, Plant Lore, Fishing, Bug Lore, and Mining)
4096 different ways a player can build their character, since players can pick anywhere from 0 to 10 skills.
719 Unique Ingredients
378 Unique consumables
176 different kinds of seeds and plants

Quests and Friendlies in Villagers and Heroes:
452 unique Quests spread across the current 3 available realms. This does not include daily quests or charters.
1275 unique variations of charters (infinite quests) spread over 130 charter types and ranks.
1144 unique daily tasks spread over 136 unique daily quests.
915 Friendly NPC’s, 263 of which are not human!
20,000+ unique lines of dialog across the world.

Villages:
117 Unique Villages across our current servers (with the number growing daily)
Over 7,000 houses on the live servers (with the number growing daily)
175,500 places to plant a seed!
39 Billion Gold (38,805,979,859) spent by players on improving villages since village projects went live.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Hallo,

wir haben gedacht, dass es einige von Euch sicherlich interessiert, ein paar Zahlen zu Villagers and Heroes zu erfahren. Wir haben Euch deswegen ein paar der interessantesten aus verschiedenen Kategorien zusammengestellt:

Spieler:
• 362.000 Charaktere wurden seit dem Spielstart 2011 erstellt.

Ausrüstung, Talente und Zauber:
• 10.566 unterschiedliche Zauber, Talente und Effekte
• 43.000 verschiedene Wege, in der sich jede Klasse die Schnellzugriffsleiste mit den jeweiligen Talenten und Zaubern bestücken kann. 
• 1.938.816.000 verschiedene Gnomifizierungsmöglichkeiten pro Klasse (ungefähr).
• 9198 verschiedene Gegenstände
• 1078 verschiedene Waffen
• 3847 verschiedene Ausrüstungsgegenstände (Rüstung, Schilde, Outfits, Schmuck)

Die Welt und seine Monster:
• 1393 unterschiedliche Kopfgeldbosse, davon 28 Ältestenbosse 
• 110 verschiedene Zonen, nicht eingeschlossen die 117 untrschiedlichen Spielerdörfer, die momentan auf den Live Servern existieren.
• 231 unterschiedliche Zingara (selten spawnende Monster).
• 2449 unterschiedliche normale Monster
• 13.303 verschiedene Orte, an denen die Bösewichter spawnen können 

Handwerk:
• 1381 unterschiedliche Rezepte in den 4 unterschiedlichen Handwerksfähigkeiten (Schneidern, Schmieden, Kochen, Holzbearbeitung) 
• 6 Sammelfähigkeiten (Gärtnern, Viehzucht, Pflanzenkunde, Insektenkunde, Bergbau und Fischen)
• 4096 verschiedene Wege, wie man als Spieler seinen Charakter aufbauen kann, da man pro Charakter die Auswahl aus bis zu 10 Fähigkeiten hat.
• 719 unterschiedliche Zutaten
• 378 unterschiedliche Vewrbrauchsgüter
• 176 verschiedene Samen- und Pflanzenarten

Quests und NPCs in Villagers and Heroes:
• 452 einzigartige Quests, verteilt auf die drei unterschiedlichen Reiche. Nicht eingeschlossen sind dabei tägliche Quests und Charter.
• 1275 unterschiedliche mögliche Charter (unendliche Quests), aufgeteilt auf 130 Charter Typen und Ränge.
• 1144 einzigartige tägliche Aufgaben, aufgeteilt auf 136 unterschiedliche tägliche Quests.
• 915 befreundete NPC, 263 davon sind nicht einmal menschlich! 
• 20,000+ Zeilen Dialog, wenn man alle NPCs in der welt zusammenzählt.

Dörfer:
• 117 unterschiedliche Spielerdörfer auf allen Servern (und die Zahl steigt täglich!) 
• über 7.000 Häuser auf allen Servern (und die Zahl steigt täglich!) 
• 175.500 Möglichkeiten, Samen zu pflanzen! (und, ihr habt richtig geraten, die Zahl steigt täglich!)

The Players:
362,000 characters have been created since Villagers and Heroes launched in 2011.
 
Gear, Feats, and Spells:
10,566 unique Spells, Feats, and Effects (including various ranks) 
43,000 different ways in which each class can choose to fill up their action bar with the 72 spells and feats available. This does not include ranks, which would make the number astronomically higher.
1,938,816,000 different ways that each class can use Gnogmenting to set up their gear with (rough estimate).
9198 Unique Items
1078 Different Weapons
3847 Different pieces of gear (belts, gloves, boots, outfits, hats, shields, rings, amulets)

The World and Monsters:
1393 Unique Bounty Bosses, 28 of which are Elder Bosses
110 Unique Zones, not including the 117 unique villages currently on live servers.
231 Unique Zingara (rare spawns).
2449 Unique normal monsters
13,303 separate locations for the baddies of the world to spawn

Crafting:
1381 unique recipes across 4 Crafting Skills (Tailoring, Smithing, Cooking, Woodcrafting)
6 Gathering skills (Gardening, Ranching, Plant Lore, Fishing, Bug Lore, and Mining)
4096 different ways a player can build their character, since players can pick anywhere from 0 to 10 skills.

notes.title: Monster Monday: Leechwood
notes.content:
Every Monday we release a new featured Bounty Boss, sharing a bit of lore and information about the Seven Realms most treacherous creatures. We are sharing our backlog of Monster Mondays for our Steam users to enjoy. 

http://i.imgur.com/4gDmQhx.png

Leechwood
Race: Tree
Location Maiden


When Maiden, infused with arcane magic’s broke from the snowy peaks of Stormhold, it caused quite the stir in much of the local fauna. And like most vegetation in Maiden, Leechwood absorbed a unique palette of magical qualities. 

The benefits of this magical imbuement were that he of course became strong and powerful, with a thick sturdy trunk, and deep growing roots.  His newly amassed branches were infused with strength, causing his boughs to swing with purpose and aim. His bark hardened, becoming impenetrable to all but the most skilled arrows and swords.

But as with most magic, there were some setbacks, the foremost being that most of his leaves fell off. While some might think that Leechwood was simply going through a season, the harsh truth was that Leechwood was now bald, something that he would be ridiculed greatly for through the whispers of the gossiping trees.

However the single most interesting thing that this magical concurrence performed on Leechwood, could be seen as a benefit, or a detriment; depending on the pondering party. Leechwood pulled his trunk from the ground for the first time, put one root in front of the other, and became what most people would call, alive.

notes.title: Class Builds: Fire Wizard
notes.content:
http://i.imgur.com/WnJ532R.jpg

Full Size Image

Hello Everyone, Diet here. 

Today we are going to get into the nitty gritty and talk about one of the many specs that a player can become, the Fire Wizard!

The Lore
Fire Wizards, like all wizards, are students of their ancient elder, Calypso. Calypso was the first of their order, and master over both fire and ice. It was Calypso who first discovered how to weave the elements together, finding that the elements worked just as well side by side as they did against one another. Additionally, it was Calypso’s closest friend, the Sentinel Kalisar, who first discovered that the wizards could harness the powers of the physical plane, developing such spells as Spirit Orb, Strike, and Shockwave. The two of them together created most of the spells that modern day wizards so potently wield. 

Overview
Wizards in general have several different ways they can specialize (spec). Wizards can spec pure Fire, pure Ice, Frostfire hybrid, Physical (aka the battle mage), or one of the many other variations. Each spec, just like all classes and build types, has its own set of strengths and weaknesses, the fire wizard being no exception.
Briefly, on the high level…

Fire Wizard Strengths:
High damage potential
Large AOE damage (area of effect)
Sustainable AOE crowd control (stuns)
Excellent addition to parties and groups
Fire Wizard Weaknesses:
High spirit consumption
Vulnerable in close range
Not quite as adept at Solo play as other build types

Fire Wizards have the potential for high burst damage with large amounts of AOE. In a group setup where a tank can pull a collection of mobs together, the fire wizard can absolutely decimate his or her foes. With long-ranged AOE spells (spells that have a radius dependent on the target rather than the caster), the fire wizard can stay out of harm’s way while dropping meteors and infernos onto the heads of their enemies. 

Additionally, with the use of skills like Fire Burst and Shockwave, fire wizards can stun groups of enemies that manage to close the gap and threaten the wizard’s position. With a well-timed fire burst matched with shockwave for backup, a smart fire wizard can almost always keep an enemy at bay.

And while fire wizards excel heavily at AOE damage, this doesn’t mean their single target damage suffers. With an entire arsenal of spells aimed at single targets, the fire wizard can let fly a lethal storm of scorching damage that will burn their foes to a crisp. 

The fire wizard does have a few drawbacks. The fast casting capability of the fire wizard often leaves them low on spirit. Some fire wizards choose to spec into Spirit Charm to help compensate, or possibly level up their skill in Cooking and Gardening so they can brew spirit regeneration potions. 

Additionally, with the low defenses of this build, the fire wizard does need to be careful how they select their battles. If a fire wizard goes into an area with spells-a-blazin’, they risk attracting too many enemies, and can be quickly overwhelmed. This is obviously is not a problem in a party or group situation, but in solo play the fire wizard does need to play smart, which sometimes can slow their pace. 

Gameplay
Now to go into the details; I have gone through a few situations to give an idea how the fire wizard can be played. These of course are only the few of many different rotations, all dependent on player choice and play style. 

Casting Rotation: Multiple Enemies
While fighting groups, the fire wizard wants to pull down as much chaos as possible, and as fast as possible. The faster the enemies fall, the safer the wizard becomes.

Leading the charge, I would suggest dropping a Flaming Meteor. This potent spell summons a meteor from the cosmos that lands in a molten blast on the enemy. The meteor explodes, dealing fire damage in a large radius and applying a burning damage over time effect to all enemy creatures hit.

Immediately after the meteor lands, you will have a swarming angry mass of enemies coming at you. Right on the heels of the meteor, throwing out an Inferno is a great way to get another hard AOE hit in.

Usually you can squeeze one more spell in before your enemies are on you. I like to pick one of the harder targets and throw out a Fireball. This ensures extra damage on the more dangerous targets.

At this point you will be surrounded by angry burning monsters, all of which want you as a dinner. This is where your Fire Burst spell comes in. Fire burst releases a ring of fire in a small radius surrounding you. As long as the enemies are within a reasonable level, your Fire Burst has 100% chance to stun the enemies for 7 seconds. This gives you ample time to finish off the baddies before they can finish off you.

If the enemy group happens to be a bit of a tougher group, shockwave can save your hide. Shockwave is the physical form of the Fire Burst (based on the research of the famous Sentinel Kalisar). Shockwave won’t do as much damage as your fire burst (since it isn’t augmented with fire damage), but it will have the same chance to stun, giving you some extra time to deal with your foes. 

After a shockwave cast, your inferno spell is probably ready to be cast again. Launch a final inferno to deal with whatever is left, and follow up with some single target spells like fireball or combust, to deal with the leftover. 

Casting Rotation: Single Target
If you are facing a single, powerful foe, an optimal build and cast rotation can make the difference between life and death. 

Starting out, I would suggest Scorching Blast. This slow traveling spell takes a bit longer to reach its target, but has a powerful effect once it does. Scorching blast not only places a burning damage over time effect on the enemy, it also weakens the enemy against fire damage. That means that as soon as your scorching blast hits, every fire spell that hits that target will do extra fire damage!

As soon as your scorching blast ignites your target, follow up with a Fireball, and then a quick Combust. Fireball travels quickly, but as a missile does have a bit of travel time. Combust on the other hand is instant, as soon as the mystical runes are uttered from your lips, the enemy combusts in blazing fire. A well-timed Fireball and Combust, just on the heels of a Scorching Blast can absolutely obliterate your target. 

If after all that the enemy still manages to make its way to your location, a fire burst can halt them in their tracks, giving you ample time to launch another one-two punch combo with Fireball and Combust. 

For some added flavor, throw in a Spirit Orb on occasion. Spirit orb is a projectile orb of pure spirit pulled from its caster. While the spirit cost of Spirit Orb is extremely high, its damage is immense. Additionally, after your Spirit Orb blasts its target, the spirit fades into the nether, where you the Wizard can collect it again. A wizard can reclaim 80% of the spirit used to cast the orb over the course of 60 seconds. 

Conclusion
The fire wizard has a few weaknesses, but those are more than compensated for with their high damage potential, and quick-casting stun capability. The fire wizard is a great spec to try out on your wizard, and in general the wizard class is loads of fun. So what are you waiting for? Create a wizard and strut your stuff. Build them how you want to, and show us your build!

What you do is up to you. Who will you become?

notes.title: Monster Monday: Wrinkles
notes.content:
Every Monday we release a new featured Bounty Boss, sharing a bit of lore and information about the Seven Realms most treacherous creatures. We are sharing our backlog of Monster Mondays for our Steam users to enjoy. 

https://i.imgur.com/7mIIIMo.png 

 Wrinkles 
 Race: Troll
Location: Sea Caves, Realm of Ardent

Though his nose was bulbous and his yellowish fangs protruded crudely from his hairy little mouth, Burkle was nonetheless rather handsome for a troll. Maybe it was his youth. His warty skin, though bumpy, was unmarked by the ravages of time and his blood red eyes sparkled with a lively zest. He was a gentle troll, and an aspiring poet for which the other trolls derisively mocked him. But Burkle didn’t care. He would much rather wander the rocky sea cliffs composing lengthy sonnets in his head than sit around a muddy cave all day plotting yet another attack on the neighboring goblins. The volatile feud existing between trolls and goblins had been going on for as long as Burkle could remember, and it bored him entirely.

Each day he would wander a little further to get away from the noisy strife of their skirmishes. One afternoon, in a scenically isolated cove, ideal for solitary poets, Burkle was startled to find that he was not alone. He had brought no weapons, only parchment and paper, so he was at first fearful of the lone goblin hovering ominously on the banks of the shore. But then she slowly turned around. Burkle was struck helpless by her beauty – her green scaly body, so lithe and slender, and her great pointy ears which flapped gently from the sides of her tiny bald head like a delicate winged butterfly. Lavinia’s golden eyes met Burkle’s, and troll and goblin were in love.

Their forbidden romance soared. A bliss-filled month of secret trysts went by. Lavinia adored her sensitive, handsome troll, and Burkle worshipped his goblin goddess. Such was their all consuming passion, however, that they soon grew careless and forgot to be mindful of secrecy. Grogan, Burkle’s father, a militant troll with a barbarous temper, learned of his son’s atrocious liaison with an enemy goblin and hurled Burkle into a dank pit. Grogan ordered his son to renounce his love for Lavinia. But Burkle adamantly refused, and, so, was kept in the pit.

He could bear the cold and the foulness, but not the separation from his beloved. Burkle grew despondent. His little sister, Tulla, took pity on him and offered to secretly deliver letters to Lavinia. Overjoyed, but wary of his father’s wrath should he find out, Burkle thought it best to use invisible ink, as only trolls can do. He zestfully sliced and gashed his arms with a jagged rock until enough troll blood had been produced with which to write the invisible letter with. As instructed, Lavinia carefully sprinkled ground mushroom dust over the parchment and watched as Burkle’s glorious words leapt into view. She vowed to love him always, and a secret written correspondence between the two began.

Despite the misery of the dank pit, the captive poet knew only joy. Sonnet after sonnet flowed from Burkle, as did his blood, which mattered little to him since the regenerative healing power of trolls ensured the rapid mending of his wounds. Burkle happily sliced and gashed himself, pounded his head against walls, and wrote epoch poems, thousands, to his beloved Lavinia, who always faithfully responded in turn. And so it was that a year passed in this way, for Burkle staunchly refused to renounce his love for Lavinia, and his militant father likewise refused to let him out of the pit.

But Grogan did fall ill one day. In his feverish delirium, he called for his son. The trolls released Burkle, who, blinking, stunned, and exhilarated, went straight to the remote cove where he knew his beloved Lavinia would come to him. And she did. Lavinia screamed in horror at sight of Burkle. His once supple young body was now a twisted mass of shriveled skin and hideous wrinkles that sagged grotesquely from every inch of him. Burkle ardently declared his love and tried to kiss her. But when his leathery, gnarled lips drew close, Lavinia violently recoiled and shrieked that she could never love such a vile wrinkled beast as he. She fled from Burkle, never to return.

His gentle soul crushed, Burkle, or ‘Wrinkles,’ as he is now often jeeringly called, wanders the lonely sea caves, a forlorn and cynical troll. He no longer writes poetry, for when faithless Lavinia went, so, too, did his love of writing go. He does nothing now, and wants only to be left alone. So beware all those who intrude upon this brooding wrinkled troll. He takes unkindly to visitors.

But Grogan did fall ill one day. In his feverish delirium, he called for his son. The trolls released Burkle, who, blinking, stunned, and exhilarated, went straight to the remote cove where he knew his beloved Lavinia would come to him. And she did. Lavinia screamed in horror at sight of Burkle. His once supple young body was now a twisted mass of shriveled skin and hideous wrinkles that sagged grotesquely from every inch of him. Burkle ardently declared his love and tried to kiss her. But when his leathery, gnarled lips drew close, Lavinia violently recoiled and shrieked that she could never love such a vile wrinkled beast as he. She fled from Burkle, never to return.

His gentle soul crushed, Burkle, or ‘Wrinkles,’ as he is now often jeeringly called, wanders the lonely sea caves, a forlorn and cynical troll. He no longer writes poetry, for when faithless Lavinia went, so, too, did his love of writing go. He does nothing now, and wants only to be left alone. So beware all those who intrude upon this brooding wrinkled troll. He takes unkindly to visitors.

notes.title: Monster Monday: Possumis
notes.content:
Every Monday we release a new featured Bounty Boss, sharing a bit of lore and information about the Seven Realms most treacherous creatures. We are sharing our backlog of Monster Mondays for our Steam users to enjoy. 

http://i.imgur.com/aPdeGt4.png

Possumis
Race: Wererodent
Location: Sawmill


Tall and mangy with a twitching rat-like face, Possumis, like most Wererodents, was a keen hoarder of discarded bobbles. But unlike his miserly peers who were content to do little else in life other than sit atop their moldy piles of rubbish in greedy silence, Possumis had far grander dreams and a much livelier tongue. He loved to talk and was particularly gifted at spinning fantastical yarns. His imagination crackled and soared, as did his ambitions, for the young Wererodent’s eyes had long been fixed upon the glimmering horizon where unexplored lands and exotic adventures awaited him. Consequently he hoarded not rubbish, but useful items he would need for his upcoming journey, all of which carefully went into the hefty rucksack Possumis wore across his furry broad shoulders.

One afternoon, needing only a few more odds and ends for his trip and growing more thrilled by the minute, Possumis decided to scavenge around the bustling sawmill in search of stray tools. But as sightings of gargantuan Wererodents strolling about in the middle of the day tended to produce hysteria, he thought it prudent to while away the hours in a nearby shed until nighttime. It was a dingy little building with rotting floorboards, several of which promptly crumbled beneath Possumis’ heavy tread, sending him tumbling down into darkness, where he landed with a painful thud upon the muddy ground of what appeared to be a forgotten earthen cellar.

Squinting and limping about, trying to get his bearings, Possumis blindly stepped right into the metallic jaws of a steely Wererodent trap which snapped firmly shut, clamping its silver teeth into his meaty leg. Possumis howled in agony, but his drastic injury soon felt trivial in comparison to the direness of his circumstances. Panic set in. He frantically heaved and pulled, then tried attacking the rusty metal beast with every gadget in his rucksack, but it was no use. He was hopelessly stuck in the cruel trap, and going nowhere at all.

When the little girl appeared in the darkness, Possumis, starving and wretched, his leg black with rot, couldn’t even guess how many weeks had passed, for he’d long since stopped counting them. There was little left of Possumis. But something like joy flickered in him, and he managed to smile at the little girl with the bright red hair and the gentle eyes who hovered shyly above him with a softly lit candle in her hand. He saw that, rather like him, she was in poor shape. Thin and sickly, her pale face was smeared with dirt as was her tattered dress. Despite her frailty, she tried to release the trap confining him. When she could not, the child wept and sank miserably to the ground. Possumis hoarsely consoled her, and asked her name. He learned it was Bronwen, and that she needed a place to hide.

Her words pained him, and Possumis longed to rip and claw at the vile goblin Bronwen’s pitiless father had sold her to. The young Wererodent fervently told her as much, and went on to provide the girl with a lengthy account of the colorfully macabre plans he had in store for the goblin. Bronwen smiled, and to Possumis’ added delight, even giggled. He thought a moment, but grew suddenly bashful, for he was after all a frightening creature. Still, Possumis shyly asked his new friend anyway. Would she like to go on a trip with him?

Possumis’ nimble paws quickly fashioned a small rucksack for Bronwen, which she excitedly filled with nothing but plump pastries, and, after quickly disposing of the vile goblin followed by a brief detour to the stone house atop the hill to watch the Royal Guards arrest her father, Possumis and Bronwen, rucksacks securely fastened, thrillingly directed their steps toward the glimmering horizon and set forth on what was to become a truly glorious journey together.

The old widow thought for sure the poor beast caught in the rusted trap was dead. But Possumis stirred. As it had been some months since she’d last checked her traps, she marveled at how any creature could have survived for so long, all alone and in the dark. The widow was irritated with herself though, for the Wererodent was by now just a desiccated pile of skin and bones and his shriveled pelt would bring her nothing. She decided not to club him, and sprang the trap open instead. But the beast didn’t move, just kept whispering gibberish to an invisible little girl next to him. The old widow impatiently nudged the Wererodent out of the trap with her foot, and told him to be off.

Possumis can often be glimpsed wandering about in the vicinity of the dingy little shed. Though he has never left the area, and likely never will, he and his friend Bronwen continue to happily explore mysterious and exciting new lands together, and such sights they have seen! One can only imagine.

notes.title: Meet the Team of Mad Otter
notes.content:
Meet the Team of Mad Otter

Hello Everyone!

We’re located in Eugene, Oregon, in the Northwest corner of the USA.  Eugene is a town of 150,000 people.  It is home to a surprising number of game developers.  It has more game developers than any other city between Seattle and the San Francisco Bay area.

We picked our name Mad Otter when we watched a  video of a tribe of otters chasing away a large crocodile from the local watering hole.  The crocodile was too large, too slow, and most importantly, too cold-bolded to compete with the more agile (and fun-loving) otters.  This was a metaphor for the kind of studio we wanted to build. 

Damon Slye -- Director, Designer
http://i.imgur.com/gKkIqwR.jpg
Damon has been building games since 1978.  In 1983, he co-founded Dynamix, a successful game studio that grew to 200 employees.  Dynamix built games at the forefront of design innovation and technology, and had the most advanced 3D engine at the time.  He is best known for creating a popular series of historic flight simulations that included Red Baron, A-10 Tank Killer, and Aces of the Pacific.  At Dynamix, he led the development of many of its core technologies, including its 3D engine.  His gameography includes Red Baron, Arcticfox, Stellar 7, MechWarrior, A10 Tank Killer, Abrams Battletank, Project Firestart, Aces of the Pacific, Aces Over Europe, Ace of Aces, and Villagers and Heroes.

Paul Bowman -- Programmer
http://i.imgur.com/lcLkhyM.jpg
Paul has been leading the development of games for over 30 years.  He has specialized in building technologically advanced games like simulations, first-person shooters, and MMOs.  He was a Lead Engineer at Dynamix and Sony.  His gameography includes Syphon Filter: Dark Mirror, Syphon Filter: Combat Ops, Syphon Filter: Logan’s Shadow, Red Baron, Aces of the Pacific, Nova 9, Project Firestart, MechWarrior, MetalTech, and Villagers and Heroes.

Liam Ryan -- Programmer
http://i.imgur.com/oF8W9NI.jpg
At the age of 10 Liam received a book of programming from his father, and has been programming ever since. After working with GarageGames and Top Meadow on such games as Marble Blast, Minigolf Mania, and Puzzle Poker (not to mention on innumerable personal projects) Liam joined Mad Otter in 2011.

Cameron England -- Designer
http://i.imgur.com/QrpNCqcs.png
Cameron has been working with Mad Otter as lead content designer for 2 years. He is a graduate of the excellent Game Development program at Lane Community College. Cameron especially loves world creation and system design, but also enjoys story writing, boss scripting, and filling the world with wonderful and kooky characters. Cameron has been playing games since his first Windows 3.1 computer, and has always had a particular fascination for RPG’s and MMO’s. 


Chris Fulkerson -- Artist
http://i.imgur.com/vNKvFgB.png
Chris has a background in both traditional and digital art and has always had a passion for games and art. He enjoys painting both on the computer and with actual paint.  He graduated from the University of Oregon Digital Arts program in 2012 and started working full time with Mad Otter shortly after.  For the past two years he's been working on the art of Villagers & Heroes as well as the new Red Baron game. For Chris, bringing together all the details in a fantasy world and increasing immersion is one of the best parts of the job.

Adam Alexander -- Artist
https://i.imgur.com/k0Syg0c.jpg
Joining Mad Otter in the summer of 2013, Adam helped both develop art content for the new "Fury of the Stone Lord," expansion and helped port the game to the upgraded engine.  He loves working on new zone environments, and in his spare time, playing bluegrass and board games.

Sarah Skibinski -- Writer
http://i.imgur.com/MFjTax1.png
Sarah joins us this year from the indie film world, where she has spent the past ten years writing a number of award winning screenplays, including ‘The Rhythm of Chaos,’ ‘The Punishing Business’, and an adaptation of Michael Dorris’ bestselling novel, ‘A Yellow Raft In Blue Water’ to name just a few.  Sarah currently writes the game lore and quests for Villagers and Heroes.

Clark Fagot -- Programmer
Clark is helping Mad Otter on a temporary basis, focusing on improving the performance of the core technology (memory usage, bandwidth, loading times).  He’s an expert in the game engine since he wrote parts of it while he worked at GarageGames.  He has his PhD in Psychology from UCSD, and Bachelor’s of Science in Mathematics and Computer Science.  He has worked at Dynamix, Brave Tree, GarageGames, and Kontagent.

We are also being very ably assisted by Ben Johnson and 
Addy Taylor
http://i.imgur.com/LR9n3Qq.jpg.  

They are doing internships through the excellent program at Lane Community College.  Ben is contributing artwork, and Addy is helping Mad Otter with promotion, and the creation of videos and other promotional assets.

Cheers!

notes.title: Monster Monday: Tokie
notes.content:
Every Monday we release a new featured Bounty Boss, sharing a bit of lore and information about the Seven Realms most treacherous creatures. We are sharing our backlog of Monster Mondays for our Steam users to enjoy.


https://i.imgur.com/4MXEOjG.png 

Tokie
Race: Rock Elemental
Location: Trader's Path

All rock elementals come from the same source, Karakcus, and Tokie is no different. 

However, being one of the more ancient rock elementals, Tokie had felt that there was much in his existence that he was missing. The flowers he attempted to pick always crushed in his grasp, and the small fleshy creatures he tried to hug  always fled or attacked him. Tokie eventually learned to be wary of offering his kindness to softer, lesser beings, and has grown bitter and jaded to any none-rock creature to cross his path.
 
Approximately 2 years after the discovery of Karackus in Hell’s furnace, some intern Monsterlogoists set about trying to capture Tokie and take him to see Karakcus, giving them the opportunity to study the encounter.  Unfortunately, they failed miserably, as moving an elemental by any means seems to be nearly impossible. 

Perhaps Tokie is, after all, still just looking for a hug?

notes.title: Monster Monday: Mystique
notes.content:
Every Monday we release a new featured Bounty Boss, sharing a bit of lore and information about the Seven Realms most treacherous creatures. We are sharing our backlog of Monster Mondays for our Steam users to enjoy.

http://i.imgur.com/ptEeFMT.png

Mystique
Race: Wraith Spider
Location: The Cathedral

In her former life, Mystique was a small town milk maid from Vinton. Mystique was the type of person that constantly harassed those around her and found everyone else inferior. Upon recollection, several locals from Vinton noted Mystique's uncanny ability at fibbing. She was known to spin elaborate webs of falsities and deceit. Everyone watched their tongues closely around Mystique, as they didn't want something that was said to be taken out of context, and blown out of proportion.

Additionally, Mystique had illustrious illusions of grandeur, and was convinced that she would eventually become someone great and wonderful. And as it turns out, she was right… but probably not how she wanted.

The Banshee Queen eventually heard tales of the fabled fibber, and chose Mystique for the exact reasons that the townspeople of Vinton detested her. The Queen needed someone who she could name as successor that would be able to keep the undead of the Southern Coast in line.

So one completely average Tuesday night (that was not at all dark, stormy, or ominous), the Banshee Queen made an offer to Mystique that couldn't be refused. She offered power, glory, authority, and everlasting life… all of the things that Mystique greatly desired.

What the Banshee Queen failed to mention to Mystique, was that the Queen had never actually done this process before. Mystique would be her first, and the Queen wasn't exactly confident about how the transformation would go.

For the most part it went great, minus the new chelicerae and a few additional legs.

Mystique is now the spider of mystery and wonder. It is forever known that Mystique was the first soul that the Banshee Queen ever extracted from a body, and she is the closest thing the Banshee Queen has to family. Mystique is now worshiped in like manner to the Queen, and has been taught the dark ways so that if anything should happen to the Banshee Queen, she may take the reigns as the terror of the Southern Coast.
